summary: This informational RFC defines the disclosure link relation type, which points to a list of IPR disclosures made about the related material.

eli5.summary: A label on a link that leads to the list of patents or claims people have declared about a document.

questions: how to link to patent disclosures
subtitle: A link type that points to intellectual property disclosures.

tldr.problem: Technical specifications sometimes relate to patents or intellectual property claims. The W3C wanted a standard way to link to the list of such disclosures, but it was never formally specified.
tldr.mechanism: Define a 'disclosure' link relation type that, when used on a resource, points to a page listing all patent or IPR disclosures related to that resource.
tldr.outcome: Web pages and technical documents can now formally declare a link to IPR disclosure lists using a standard relation type.

today: RFC 6579 is an Informational RFC. The 'disclosure' link relation is now registered with IANA and is used by W3C, IETF, and other organizations to link specifications to patent disclosure lists.

sections.title: Patent Disclosures on the Web
sections.content:
The W3C and IETF work with patents and intellectual property claims. When a specification might be covered by patents, it is important to disclose that fact. RFC 5988 defined a way to express relationships between web resources using link relation types. The 'disclosure' type was already in use at W3C and elsewhere, but it was never formally specified or registered.

This RFC formalizes the existing practice by defining 'disclosure' and registering it with IANA. The W3C already mandates its use, and this brings it into the broader IETF standard framework.
sections.eli5: Patent claims are serious. Different organizations were already linking to them, but they did it in ad-hoc ways. This makes it official and standard.

sections.title: The Disclosure Relation
sections.content:
When a resource uses the 'disclosure' link relation, the link target MUST be a list of patent disclosures or IPR disclosures made with respect to that resource. The list can be empty, contain one entry, or contain many. The relation type applies to both HTML links (via rel='disclosure' in an anchor tag) and to the Link header field in HTTP responses.

The 'disclosure' relation is distinct from the 'copyright' relation, which points to the copyright statement. Patent disclosures are IPR claims, a different kind of legal information.
sections.eli5: On a web page about a specification, you can add a link with rel='disclosure' that points to the patent list.

sections.title: Using Disclosure Links
sections.content: An HTML page can include an anchor element with rel='disclosure' to point to the list of patents. Alternatively, an HTTP response can include a Link header field with rel='disclosure' and a URL target. Both methods achieve the same result: they inform anyone viewing the specification that they should check the disclosure list for relevant patents.
sections.eli5: Either put a link on the page, or add a header to the HTTP response. Either way, readers can find the patent list.

references.text: Bradner, S., "Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels", BCP 14, RFC 2119, March 1997.
